summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 11, part 99) set at a school. Rebecca and Huldah discuss Miss Maxwell, the Latin teacher, and Rebecca says she loves her. Huldah explains she lost her Latin grammar after a quarrel with Herbert Dunn, whom she had stopped speaking to and whose class pin she returned. Emma Jane interrupts to end the talk, and Huldah describes her flashy blue dress, white trim and souvenir pins, then mentions Mr. Morrison and a handsome stranger in the office.
one_line: Schoolgirls Rebecca and Huldah argue about Miss Maxwell and Huldah's lost Latin grammar in a fiction excerpt.
key_facts: Huldah says it was Miss Maxwell's place to teach her Latin, not manners.
Rebecca tells Huldah she not only abides Miss Maxwell but loves her.
Rebecca says she would like to put a marble platform in Miss Maxwell's class-room and have her sit in a velvet chair behind a golden table.
Emma Jane asks whether Huldah's study hour is now, to stop further discussion.
Huldah lost her Latin grammar after leaving it in the hall for half an hour.
Huldah had a quarrel with Herbert Dunn and gave him back his class pin.
Huldah had not spoken to Herbert Dunn for a week before the quarrel's aftermath.
Mr. Morrison thinks the grammar will be returned and has offered to lend Huldah another.
Huldah's woolen dress had once been gray but was dyed a brilliant blue.
Huldah added three rows of white braid and large white pearl buttons to her gray jacket to make it more dressy.
Huldah's gray felt hat has a white feather, and her white tissue veil has large black dots.
Her open jacket shows a small American flag, a button of the Wareham Rowing Club, and one or two society pins.
Rebecca notices the color of Huldah's front hair has been dulled by incessant frizzing with curling irons.
Huldah describes a handsome, elegant stranger in the principal's office who seemed too young to be a father and too old to be a brother.
